blanks.sentence: Keeping good news private can make someone feel more _____, especially when they intend to tell someone later.
blanks.section: NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS — A possible benefit

blanks.sentence: A _____ is one example of something enjoyable that a person may plan never to disclose.
A surprise _____ is an example of news kept so that it can later be revealed.
Revealing welcome news gives people a chance to share and _____ it with others.
A sense of _____ over one's emotions can make a positive secret energising.
blanks.section: Why a secret can feel positive

blanks.sentence: In some cultures, people may _____ a pregnancy announcement until they feel it is safe to share.
In the early stages, a pregnancy secret may feel like a _____ to the person keeping it.

multipleChoice.question: Which contrast introduces the discussion about keeping secrets?
options: People often value privacy, although sharing news can strengthen relationships.
People often see secrecy negatively, although some secrets may improve their lives.
People often keep secrets easily, although some news is difficult to protect.
People often enjoy surprises, although keeping them can make them anxious.

multipleChoice.question: According to the studies described, when might holding on to good news feel especially positive?
options: When the news concerns a person whom the listener already knows.
When the person expects the news to remain private indefinitely.
When the person intends to share the news with someone later.
When the person has already discussed the news with friends.

multipleChoice.question: What distinguishes the two kinds of enjoyable secrets described by the researcher?
options: Whether the person intends to reveal them eventually.
Whether the news concerns a relationship or an object.
Whether other people can guess the secret beforehand.
Whether keeping the secret produces a sense of guilt.

multipleChoice.question: What effect does the presenter attribute to negative secrets?
options: They can reduce the excitement of a planned surprise.
They can make people less willing to discuss emotions.
They can prevent good news from reaching other people.
They can harm people and strain their relationships.

multipleChoice.question: Why is the location of the research raised in the discussion?
options: It may limit how confidently the findings apply to other cultures.
It explains why the study focused on marriage proposals.
It shows that secrecy is understood similarly worldwide.
It suggests that the results depend on the language spoken.

multipleChoice.question: What is the purpose of the example about delaying pregnancy news in some cultures?
options: To show that early pregnancy news is usually a negative secret.
To explain why researchers avoid asking about pregnancy.
To explore whether cultural beliefs affect decisions to share good news.
To show that all good news is best kept private until it is safe.

multipleChoice.question: How does the researcher tentatively contrast pregnancy secrets at earlier and later stages?
options: People become less concerned about others' reactions as time passes.
The same news can feel more comfortable to discuss at a later stage.
The secret becomes positive only after everyone already knows it.
Pregnancy news has a fixed emotional effect across cultures.
